text: Tens of thousands of Boston Dynamics robots going into Hyundai’s operations in next years So the rumored Boston Dynamics IPO is still only a rumor but gains a little more likelihood with the ongoing Hyundai investment preparations, and strong interest in manufacturing robots in the USA. Boston Dynamics and Hyundai have announced more details about that strategy! We also had a great Bots&Beer at Circuit Launch Mountain View this week with someone even driving all the way from Reno to show off their humanoid robot (thanks Roberto!), and other demos, including PartCAD - which is Git for physical design. Also great presentations from Nic at DeepSea Developments and Yegor of Instock Robotics. Thanks Tony D’Antonio for photos! This funding will be used to scale the deployment of our AI-enabled meal assembly robots. It's exciting times over here - demand for flexible automation is growing, and we're shipping a lot of robots. I've attached a press release with full details of the round. Here's the story CNBC published: Chef Robotics raises $20.6 million to continue building AI robot arms ($20.6M is the total figure without debt raised included) Here's the official press release with full details of the funding round: Chef Robotics Announces $43M Series A Round Led by Avataar Ventures to Scale the Deployment of AI-Enabled Robotics Here's a blog we wrote that tells the story of how we got here, and how the funding will be used: We’ve Raised a $43M Series A to Accelerate Our AI-Enabled Robot Deployments How China’s interlinking ecosystem helps robotics NYSE Wired Robotics & AI Media Week TheCUBE's coverage of the NYSE Wired Robotics & AI Media Week highlighted the transformative impact of robotics and artificial intelligence across various sectors. Key discussions centered around advancements in manufacturing, the integration of AI in robotics, and the evolving landscape of technology and finance. Industry leaders shared insights on how these technologies are bridging gaps between virtual and physical worlds, emphasizing collaboration, innovation, and sustainability as critical components for future growth. 30 plus interviews on demand with robotics CEOs like Jeff Cardenas, Tobin Fisher, Saman Farid, Jack Morrison, Noah Ready Campbell, and companies like Bright Machines, Machina Labs, Elroy Air, Brain Corp, Dexterity and more.
